syllabusTopics: Limits and continuity: limits of a function, indeterminate forms, algebraic properties of limits (without proof), basic theorems on limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
Derivatives: derivative of a function, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions by definition (simple forms)
Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives
Geometric interpretation of derivative; monotonicity of a function, interval of monotonicity, extreme values of a function, concavity, points of inflection
Anti-derivatives: integration using basic integrals, integration by substitution and by parts methods
The definite integral; the definite integral as an area under the given curve; area between two curves

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Treating every solution of $f'=0$ as a maximum or a minimum.  ·  Forgetting the two endpoints when finding absolute extrema on a closed interval.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Where a formula is quoted it is valid only under the conditions stated; Treating every solution of $f'=0$ as a maximum or a minimum.  ·  Every result here follows from the definitions, so a first-principles derivation is always a valid fallback in the exam.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The terrace point*** - x^3 at 0: stationary, sign of f' unchanged, no extremum - the zero alone never classifies.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Checking $f'$ at a single point instead of across the interval when deciding monotonicity.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Work through the authored practice problems and re-derive each key formula from the definition.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Build the sign table before classifying - the intervals, not the zeros, carry the verdicts.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): Find the intervals of increase/decrease and classify the critical points of f(x) = x³ − 3x.** — **Derivative:** f′ = 3x² − 3 = 3(x − 1)(x + 1); zeros at x = ±1; f′ exists everywhere ⟹ candidates {−1, 1}.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Classify the critical points of f(x) = x⁴ − 4x³ using the second-derivative test, noting any inconclusive cases.** — **Derivative:** f′ = 4x³ − 12x² = 4x²(x − 3); candidates x = 0 and x = 3. **Second derivative:** f″ = 12x² − 24x = 12x(x − 2). **At x = 3:** f″(3) = 36 > 0 ⟹ **local min** at (3, −27).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: In optimisation, close with a context sentence: units, the answer's meaning, and why it is the max/min.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Fermat: f' = 0 is necessary for smooth interior extrema; the sign change is what is sufficient.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: f' > 0 => increasing; f' < 0 => decreasing (MVT promotes local signs to global). Critical points: f' = 0 OR f' fails - corners and cusps are candidates too. First-derivative test: the SIGN CHANGE classifies (+ to - max, - to + min, no change terrace). Second-derivative test: f''(c) > 0 min, < 0 max, = 0 inconclusive.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: |x| has its minimum at a point where the derivative does not exist - the candidate list must include derivative failures.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): Find the absolute maximum and minimum of f(x) = x³ − 3x on [−2, 2].** — **Candidates:** critical points from the previous analysis: x = −1, 1; **plus endpoints** x = −2, 2 (the EVT guarantees absolute extrema exist on the closed interval, and they may sit at the ends).…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): A rectangle has perimeter 40 cm. Find the dimensions that maximise its area, justifying the maximum.** — **Translate:** sides x and y with 2x + 2y = 40 ⟹ y = 20 − x, 0 < x < 20. **Objective:** A(x) = x(20 − x) = 20x − x². **Critical point:** A′ = 20 − 2x = 0 ⟹ **x = 10**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Companion Doorway to Monotonicity and Extreme Values This canonical is the **short-form doorway** to monotonicity and extreme values: sign tables, critical points, and the two tests in one page. The parent canonical carries the full treatment; this companion mirrors the theorems, adds the deep readings, and drills four heavy-mark problems.  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Monotonicity:** f′ > 0 on an interval ⟹ strictly increasing; f′ < 0 ⟹ strictly decreasing (MVT converts local signs to global behaviour). - **Critical points:** interior points where f′ = 0 or f′ fails to exist — the only candidates for local extrema.…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — The Sign Table Is the Theorem Made Mechanical - The first-derivative test is the **MVT wearing a table**: f′ > 0 on (a, c) means f climbs on that whole stretch; the sign change at c means the climb stops and a descent begins — a summit. The table's columns are intervals, its entries are the MVT's verdicts.…
